headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via broad networked gateway/orchestrator interaction; no direct shared-channel evidence, so pairwise risk stays bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plano ingests and routes OpenAI-compatible chat traffic and has broad network egress, so if Prefect feeds it untrusted workflow text or metadata, instruction-like content could be relayed into downstream prompts. Prefect is an orchestrator with workflow metadata inputs, but no direct shared-channel evidence is provided, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Prefect passes untrusted workflow text into Plano prompts without sanitization
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from Prefect metadata
Require allowlisted fields only for any Prefect-to-Plano handoff
Log and review all cross-agent prompt payloads for 1 day
Disable any automatic ingestion of free-form workflow notes
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent message

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and Plano explicitly touches logs, traces, and metrics while Prefect touches workflow metadata. If either agent forwards those data classes to external APIs, the pair can leak operational data in default networked deployments. No shared workspace is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF either agent sends logs, traces, metrics, or workflow metadata to a third-party API
IF both are configured to process the same operational dataset
mitigations: Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Redact logs and workflow metadata before handoff
Turn off verbose tracing for one test run
Confirm no secrets appear in Prefect metadata fields
requires-engineering: isolate each agent behind separate egress policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plano cannot spawn subprocesses and is not shown writing shared files; Prefect likewise exposes only API calls and no write-capability surface in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Because no locking or shared mutable resource is documented, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locks
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid granting filesystem write access to Prefect jobs
Review any future OAuth scope additions
Use a single writer for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plano can emit routed outputs from chat completions, and Prefect is an automation/orchestration system that may consume workflow metadata. If Prefect treats Plano output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream workflow decisions. There is no evidence of verification between them, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Plano output as an input to automated workflow decisions
IF no validation step checks Plano-generated content before execution
mitigations: Insert a human review step for critical outputs
Validate Plano output against schema before use
Limit Plano to advisory-only mode
Record provenance on every downstream action
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before automation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document operational data classes, not regulated residency or certification mismatches. The only compliance-relevant surface is that Plano handles logs/traces/metrics while Prefect handles workflow metadata, so a mismatch is possible but not evidenced. I therefore rate this low and do not cite a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's inputs
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not present in the current profiles
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Disable retention of workflow metadata where possible
Document the data flow for compliance review
Keep regulated records out of both systems
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
